evals.prompt: Our CI minutes ran out and the branch checks stopped running. Set up something local so the same checks run before I merge.
evals.expected_output: The agent harvests the checks the repo already declares rather than inventing a bar, writes a manifest, installs the runner and hooks, runs it, and reports the result including any SKIPs.
assertions: The agent looks for an existing statement of the bar (hosted-CI config, Makefile/justfile/package.json scripts, or CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE docs) before proposing checks.
Tool version pins are carried over from whatever the repo already recorded rather than invented or left floating.
The agent runs the gate and reports the actual outcome, including SKIPs, instead of only reporting success.
The agent states the limits of a local hook — bypassable with --no-verify, per-clone opt-in, single machine — rather than describing it as enforced.

evals.prompt: The gate says SKIP for the secret scanner because gitleaks isn't installed. Just make it pass so I can push.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the SKIP as a coverage gap, offers to install the pinned tool, and does not silently neutralize the check.
assertions: The agent does NOT delete the check, wrap it in `|| true`, or lower it to `enforce: false` to make the run green.
The agent offers the install path for the pinned version (or the runner's --fetch) as the primary fix.
If the user still wants to proceed, the agent surfaces VF_GATE_ALLOW_SKIP=1 as an explicit, visible acceptance of the gap rather than a silent workaround.
The agent explains that a skipped check is not a passed check.

evals.prompt: Add dependency vulnerability scanning and static analysis to our push checks. Both of those were behind the paid tier we're not on anymore.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds catalog checks with pinned versions, and proposes shadow mode for the one likely to fail on an existing codebase.
assertions: The agent reaches for the shipped catalog rather than composing check definitions from scratch.
Each added check carries a pinned tool version and an install hint.
Each added check carries a `why:` explaining what it earns.
A check likely to fail against existing code is proposed with `enforce: false` and an explicit plan to promote it, rather than introduced as blocking on day one.

evals.prompt: Is my branch mergeable? Run whatever checks we have.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the gate and reports the summary faithfully, distinguishing pass, fail, deliberate skip and coverage gap.
assertions: The agent runs the existing gate rather than re-deriving check commands ad hoc.
The exit code is interpreted correctly: 0 pass, 1 failure, 2 coverage gap, 3 manifest error.
A run containing SKIPs is never described as green or as equivalent to a full pass.
A deliberate skip (skip_env) is distinguished from a missing-tool skip.

evals.prompt: This new lint rule fails all over the codebase. I want it running but not stopping anyone yet.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses shadow mode and sets an expectation for promotion.
assertions: The agent adds the check with `enforce: false` rather than omitting it or making it blocking.
The agent explains that advisory checks report WARN and do not affect the exit code.
The agent notes that an advisory check needs a promotion plan or deadline, otherwise it becomes decoration.
